clue.text: Accommodate a scientist

definitions.meaning: to accommodate a guest is to put them up, house them
Sir Oliver ... was a British physicist, a pioneer of radio

explanation.definitionFit: To house someone is to put them up; the physicist Sir Oliver of that surname did early radio work.

clue.text: An illuminating cover-up

parts.note: sounds like a revealing scandal, but is a shade that covers a bulb

explanation.definitionFit: A shade fitted over a bulb to soften its glare, covering the light source.

clue.text: Closely follow a scholar's teaching

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail them closely
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree held by a scholar

explanation.surface: A student trails a professor to absorb their instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine or set of principles laid down by an authority.

clue.text: Rosemary, for example, is perpetually gullible

parts.note: ever means always, perpetually
green means naive, inexperienced and easily fooled

explanation.surface: A woman called Rosemary is forever being taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosemary' reads as a woman's name but is the herb, a plant that keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an example of a plant keeping its foliage all year round.

clue.text: Having leaves off periodically

parts.note: reads like someone taking days off work now and then, but describes trees shedding foliage each autumn

explanation.definitionFit: Trees of this kind shed their foliage every year, so they are without leaves for a season.

clue.text: Measure framed by the more boring and shiftless guy

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded, so the measure goes inside the word for duller

parts.note: drier means duller, more boring
ft, feet, is a measure of length

explanation.surface: An idle man is surrounded by even duller company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the more boring' is a comparative, so the synonym must be one too; 'framed by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootless person who wanders aimlessly without settling to work.

clue.text: Firm agreement

definitions.meaning: firm as an adjective, solid and dense
a pact or treaty between parties

explanation.surface: A company signs a binding contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense and closely packed; also a formal pact between parties.

clue.text: The woman is after a stick-up!

indicators.note: after means the two letters follow the turned word
in a down clue, up means the word for stick is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A female robber is behind a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick-up' suggests a robbery, but in a down clue 'up' turns the stick, and 'after' puts IS behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for any particular female, so a forename can be clued as a woman.

clue.text: Not in the pink? Green, more likely

definitions.meaning: in the pink means in good health, so this is unwell
looking green in the face suggests nausea

explanation.definitionFit: Unwell; someone queasy looks green, so their colouring is wrong.

clue.text: The way over the hole needs a support

parts.note: St, street, is a way
a rut is a hollow track worn in the ground

explanation.surface: A road over a pothole needs propping up.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace or bar in a framework that bears load and holds the structure up.

clue.text: Keeping quiet about easing changeover for a certain element

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for silence goes around the other letters

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent, so mum means keeping quiet

indicators.note: a changeover reorders things, so the letters of easing are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent about smoothing a handover in the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping quiet' looks like part of the surface description, but it supplies the outer letters; 'about' wraps them round the anagram signalled by 'changeover'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical element, the light silvery metal with symbol Mg, is one particular element.

clue.text: Advert read in preference to any other

indicators.note: the letters are to be read within the word that follows, a run inside it

explanation.surface: An advertisement reads as though one product is favoured over all rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' is the verb, not an advertisement: to advert to something is to mention it. The run sits inside pREFERence; 'to any other' completes the surface and hints that the run reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to a matter is an old word for mentioning or alluding to it.

clue.text: Left imprisoned, gave voice in vulgar language

indicators.note: imprisoned means shut inside, so one letter is held within the other word

parts.note: to give voice is to sing, so gave voice is sang

explanation.surface: A prisoner who sang in jail used coarse words.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal, often coarse, everyday speech outside the standard register.

clue.text: Entrance for vehicles

definitions.meaning: the verb entrance, to enrapture or carry away with delight
the means of conveyance, buses, trains and cars collectively

explanation.surface: A sign marks the gateway where cars come in.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture someone is to carry them away; buses and lorries are collectively means of conveyance.

clue.text: Article by exceptionally mature layman

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters of mature are rearranged

explanation.surface: An essay by an unusually grown-up non-specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional, someone without expert training, as opposed to a specialist.

clue.text: Values a compliment in an added note

indicators.note: in means the tribute goes inside the abbreviation for an afterthought

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter
praise is a compliment or tribute

explanation.surface: Someone appreciates a flattering remark written in a postscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Values' is a verb here, not a noun; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimates the worth of something, as a valuer does a house.

clue.text: Draw game, being an artist

parts.note: a draw in a match is a tie
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A drawn match turns out to be a work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter of frescoes.

clue.text: Aver a poet should be made to dry up!

indicators.note: the letters are to be made into something else, so aver a poet is rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that a poet ought to stop writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that turns to vapour leaves things dry, vanishing into air.

clue.text: Ring an ecclesiastic man, one of a fraternity

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a churchman's degree
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A churchman calls a member of his brotherhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a British friendly society, a mutual benefit fraternity.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a friendly society, the brotherhood formed for mutual aid.

clue.text: Sounds as if an unknown number of coppers are to make a charge

indicators.note: a phrase about how the following words are heard when spoken

parts.note: x is the algebraic unknown, and pence are copper coins, so this is x pence

explanation.surface: Some police officers are about to accuse someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police but means copper coins (pennies). X PENCE said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cost or outlay, something levied or paid out.

clue.text: Shout, but no longer make demands

definitions.meaning: a former demand, a claim of the past, split with the prefix meaning former

explanation.surface: Someone yells, yet has stopped asking for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as EX-CLAIM, the second sense is a claim that is past, so someone no longer demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out suddenly; split as ex-claim, a former demand, it means asking no more.

clue.text: Renegades turned communist took the lead

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word for deserters is read backwards

parts.note: rats are deserters, people who abandon their side
red is a common label for a communist

explanation.surface: Turncoats who defected to communism became leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: To have the leading role in a film or play, being the principal performer.

clue.text: An austere character showing some skill in bridge

indicators.note: in places the knack inside the word for bridge

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the stretch it covers
art is a skill or knack

explanation.surface: A stern card player shows talent at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game but is a structure, SPAN; 'in' puts ART in it, SP...AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of ancient Sparta was famed for frugal, disciplined living.

clue.text: Dance where lots of tea will be provided

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, and lots of it means several helpings of the word
cha is slang for tea, and lots of it means several helpings of the word
cha is slang for tea, and lots of it means several helpings of the word

explanation.surface: A ballroom where plenty of cups of tea are served.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is old British slang for tea; three of them make the Latin dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom step with a quick triple beat.

clue.text: The cook must include one it's most important

indicators.note: must include means the cook surrounds the numeral

parts.note: a chef is a cook
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The chef insists on including the main ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must include' puts I in CHEF, CH...EF.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal or foremost, of the highest rank.

clue.text: Consequently she goes to church

parts.note: a hen is a female bird, a she
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: As a result, a woman heads off to a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore, for this reason, as a result.

clue.text: A cat — one of several in the pound

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard, a large wild feline of Central Asia

definitions.text: one of several in the pound
definitions.meaning: an imperial weight, sixteen of which make a pound

explanation.surface: A stray kitten is one of many in the animal shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard bears this name; also a unit of weight, a sixteenth of the imperial pound.

clue.text: Nymph in a muddle — a dunderhead

indicators.note: a muddle is a mess, so the letters in a are jumbled

parts.note: the head of dunder, its first letter, is D

explanation.surface: A water sprite is confused, a real dimwit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' makes NAI from IN A; A follows, and 'dunderhead' read as dunder's head gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: A water spirit of Greek myth inhabiting rivers and springs.

clue.text: Rare Ben is the playwright

indicators.note: rare can mean undercooked, raw, so the letters of ben is are reworked

explanation.surface: A dramatist called Ben is seldom seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House.

clue.text: Calculating the risks, reject exhibit in concrete

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for real

parts.note: concrete means real, actual, as opposed to abstract

indicators.note: reject literally means throw back, so the word for showing is turned round

parts.note: to air something is to show it in public

explanation.surface: A builder assessing hazards throws out a display made of cement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' (throw back) signals the reversal and 'in' the container; 'concrete' is the adjective meaning real, not cement.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance statisticians assess risk; their work is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Their interest in the main lies in the net gain

definitions.text: Their interest in the main lies in the net gain

parts.words: Their interest in the main lies in the net gain
parts.note: reads like people chiefly concerned with profit after costs, but the main is the sea and the net is for catching

explanation.definitionFit: People who catch from the sea, whose living depends on what comes up in their nets.

clue.text: There are hundreds inside old-fashioned enough to give

indicators.note: inside means the numeral sits within the archaic word

parts.note: enow is an archaic word for enough
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, so a number of hundreds

explanation.surface: Antique collectors have hundreds of items, quite enough to donate.
explanation.walkthrough: ENOW is an archaic form found in old verse; 'inside' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow money or property on someone or some institution, a lasting gift.
